content:
Pri: Deal update  enterprise wants processing residency in DE (Frankfurt) with deterministic failover to CA (Montreal). They will not accept any control-plane traffic through US. BYOK via customer HSM in their cloud required. Need quick callouts: subprocessors, routing policy, and what to quote for POC.
Julian: Short answer: hosted public API uses US control plane; that fails requirement. Two viable POC paths: (1) Redwood Private (control plane deployed into customer VPC) or (2) Dedicated with regional control-plane (longer lead). Recommend Private for speed.
Monica: Data path: we can tenant-pin compute to eu-central-1 and set deterministic failover to ca-central-1. Important: default telemetry and some analytics jobs may hit central endpoints unless telemetry_exports disabled.
Therese: Compliance checklist: produce subprocessor register (legal names + country). AWS staff in DE and GCP staff in CA will be subprocessors depending on provider mapping. We must confirm that support/debug tooling does not route secrets or logs via US services for this tenant.
Pri: Customer clarified keys: they will manage keys in their ca-central-1 HSM and do not want Redwood to host keys.
Monica: Good  customer-managed BYOK reduces legal friction. Technical checklist for POC:
- VPC peering/PrivateLink or equivalent
- Mutual TLS for control-plane endpoints
- Service account with narrow IAM roles
- KMS grant + key policy review and rotation notes
- Telemetry export disablement and egress ACLs
Julian: Sample routing config for POC to show buyer: 
```nrouting:
  residency:
    tenant_id: X-ACME
    primary_region: eu-central-1
    failover_region: ca-central-1
    control_plane_placement: customer_vpc
    telemetry_exports: false
```
Therese: Legal will compile subprocessor list and annotate any teams or tools that have US residency. Also drafting SOW clause: "Control plane and management plane will be deployed inside customer VPC; telemetry exports disabled unless explicitly authorized; subprocessor register attached."
Pri: Customer metrics: peak bursts ~180 RPS, avg 40k tokens/day, 7d retention. They requested ballpark delta vs standard hosted pricing for: (A) 30d POC with BYOK and pinned routing, (B) Production Private or Dedicated with BYOK and SLA.
Julian: Pricing guidance: POC = one-time setup fee + light reserved capacity + egress contingency for DE<->CA failover tests. Prod = monthly platform fee + reserved commit + BYOK integration fee + optional SLA uplift. Also include estimated engineering onboarding hours.
Monica: Estimate: 30-60 eng hours for Private POC (deploy control plane, peering, KMS integration, smoke tests), POC spin-up target ~10 business days if customer provides network contacts and KMS policies quickly.
SRE-Bot: Created ticket GEO-POC-360: "FR primary / CA failover / customer BYOK" assigned to Monica for execution.
Therese: We'll also attach SOC2/ISO docs and provide a short shadowtest plan to capture flow logs proving no US transit during POC. Need SRE to extract flow logs.
Pri: Great. I'll send the buyer a summary and schedule an ops call for tomorrow. @Julian @Therese please add pricing lines and the subprocessor appendix to the deck. :white_check_mark:
